warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor. The architect, all workers, all auditors and this red team run on the same model family (claude-opus-5). Isolated contexts are not independent vendors, so an error the model is prone to can pass on both sides of every check. Only the deterministic layer really holds he

Writes to the raw sources and the frozen machinery were barred by permissions.deny, which covers the edit tools only, not the shell. A modified raw file would be caught afterwards by the control lock, not prevented.

The LLM audit layer in this run produced no independent evidence. gate0_semantic, gate_release_auditor and all four workers each report a single placeholder check (0.473684, a number that appears in no artifact of this audit) with the summary 'driver e2e', and every auditor evidence file is a one-li

Every worker result, auditor result and carry is timestamped 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. That is three months before the analysis plan was registered (2026-04-02T09:00:00Z), so the timestamps are placeholders and the order of work cannot be read from them.

No machine rule covers any of the following: customer_id, order_date and country in the clean table; the is_delivered and shipping_missing flags that every metric, estimate and test filters on; the n printed next to each estimate; report prose; dashboard card completeness; the content of analysis/an

Of the RESOLVED readings, refund_sign_policy looks the weakest. The 10 excluded in-quarter orders (8 delivered, 2 pending, 9 direct) have small negative refunds of -21.39 to -71.74 EUR on ordinary gross amounts, which looks like a sign error rather than a non-sale. Including them would raise CLM-ORD

The other RESOLVED readings hold on this export. The last row equals the latest updated_at for all 917 repeated orders; reading the first revision instead would give net revenue 3,010,704.83 and direct completion 0.722161. Slashed dates read month-first agree with order_month on all 6,852 rows, whil

The analysis plan assumes independent observations after deduplication, which is not literally true. The 44,531 orders come from 4,198 customers, 4,158 of whom order in both channels, with up to 23 orders each. However, the measured cluster design effect is only 0.99 to 1.03, so the published interv

The size of the shipping values looks wrong for EUR per order. Readable shipping cells have a median of about 905 against a gross median near 110, and 94% of them exceed the order's gross. shipping_total (37,792,722.50, unpublished) is 12.5 times net revenue. The column may not be EUR per order, whi

On both surfaces the AOV cards carry the caveat 'one quarter of orders in this channel', but the AOV population is delivered orders only (n 17,818 and 12,055 against 24,597 and 19,934 channel orders). The check plan does not require a delivered-only caveat for AOV, and on the dashboard nothing else

Both p values are rendered as 0.0000 on the report and the dashboard rather than as below 0.0001, so a reader may take p to be exactly zero. The true values are far smaller than the display precision.

release_surface_contract.json declares src/release/build_release.py as a generator source, but the release gate evidence records no generator-literal scan. src/ is outside this step's inputs, so I could not confirm that the generator holds no business literal.
The report says nothing about shipping, so a reader of release/report.md is not told that the R05 question received no published figure, or why.

Completion varies by month (direct 0.7193 to 0.7321, partner 0.5947 to 0.6163) while each channel's country mix stays near one third per country. The quarterly Wilson interval is a sampling interval and does not describe this month-to-month movement.

The handoff has no drift_since_review field. Its absence does not prove that the stage code's assumptions hold on this export; the probes in audit/results/final/evidence/assumption_probes.json are the only evidence that they do.

No decisions journal exists (audit/decisions/ is empty and rulings is empty), and no worker result has a disclosures field or any warning. So no human ruling and no self-reported deviation could be traced into the release.

The carry schema is outside this step's inputs, so the four carries were compared with the stage outputs but not validated against the schema. Retry history, stale inputs and runner state are also outside the inputs and were not checked; see audit_runner.py report.
